bib.title: Adaptive Input Representations for Neural Language Modeling

question: How should input and output layers of a self-attentional language model be factorized (word, character, sub-word, adaptive) for best accuracy and speed?
hypothesis: Giving frequent words larger embeddings and rare words smaller ones (as adaptive softmax does for outputs) reduces overfitting to rare words and parameters while improving accuracy.
contributions: Adaptive input embeddings extending adaptive softmax to inputs
Systematic comparison of word, char-CNN, BPE and adaptive factorizations
SOTA on WikiText-103 (18.7) and Billion Word (23.02)

method.summary: Decoder-only transformer language model with frequency-banded input embeddings (dimension shrinks by k=4 per band, projected to d) optionally tied with an adaptive softmax output. Compared against fixed word, BPE and char-CNN input/output layers under identical architecture.

datasets.name: Billion Word
datasets.preprocessing: words with more than 3 occurrences kept; sentences batched individually

datasets.name: WikiText-103
datasets.preprocessing: types with more than 3 occurrences; blocks of 512 contiguous tokens (3072 for headline result), ignoring document boundaries

models.name: Adaptive inputs (ADP / ADP-T)
models.hidden: e=1024 (1536 very large); FFN 4096 (6144 large, 8192 very large)

other.fixed_embedding_size: 512 WikiText-103 SM; 64 Billion Word SM; BPE 1024; ASM input 64 (WikiText-103), 256 (Billion Word)

training.optimizer: Nesterov accelerated gradient, momentum 0.99, gradient renormalized if norm exceeds 0.1
training.lr_schedule: cosine with restarts (C cycles, each twice as long as previous, max/min lowered by factor M); Billion Word C=3, first cycle 137K steps, M=0.6; WikiText-103 C=4, first cycle 18K steps, M=0.75
training.batch_size: 65K tokens effective: Billion Word B=2048 tokens/GPU x 32 GPUs (64 GPUs for main results); WikiText-103 B=4096 x 8 GPUs, 2 batches accumulated
training.seq_len: 512 (WikiText-103 default), 3072 for headline result; Billion Word per sentence
training.dropout: Billion Word 0.1 + attention 0.1; WikiText-103 0.3, ReLU dropout 0.1, attention dropout 0.1; tail dropout in adaptive softmax projection (0.2 best, Table 6)
training.regularisation: dropout in adaptive softmax tail projection; weight tying
training.hardware: DGX-1 machines with 8 NVIDIA V100 GPUs, Infiniband, NCCL2
training.wall_clock: Billion Word: 55h adaptive, 79h char-CNN, 145h very large (64 GPUs); WikiText-103: 67h (8 GPUs)

inference.samples: single run per config, no seeds stated

parameters.eval_blocks: complete sentences up to 512 tokens; headline: 3072 tokens, first 2560 as context, score last 512

metrics.name: perplexity
metrics.definition: word-level perplexity; for BPE, word probability is product of sub-word probabilities

eval.protocol: same hyperparameters per dataset; same number of updates; validation used for tuning; no seeds or significance tests
